## Running Code

```{r}

library(tidyverse)

# 1. Download NOAA's monthly SST index data
url <- "https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/data/indices/sstoi.indices"

raw <- read.table(url, header = TRUE)

# Check that the expected column names are present
stopifnot(all(c("YR", "MON", "ANOM.3") %in% names(raw)))

# ANOM.3 is the traditional monthly Niño 3.4 anomaly column
nino <- raw |>
  select(YR, MON, nino34 = ANOM.3) |>
  filter(!is.na(nino34))

# 2. Align each event to a July-June period
df <- nino |>
  mutate(
    event = if_else(MON >= 7, YR, YR - 1),
    month_idx = if_else(MON >= 7, MON - 6, MON + 6)
  ) |>
  filter(event %in% c(1982, 1997, 2015, 2026)) |>
  mutate(
    label = if_else(
      event == 2026,
      "2026 (so far)",
      as.character(event)
    )
  )

# Find the latest available 2026 observation
latest <- df |>
  filter(event == 2026) |>
  slice_max(month_idx, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

stopifnot(nrow(latest) == 1)

latest_month <- month.name[latest$MON[[1]]]

# Separate historical events from 2026
past <- df |> filter(event != 2026)
now  <- df |> filter(event == 2026)

# 3. Set colors
pal <- c(
  "1982" = "#A5BBA2",
  "1997" = "#77977B",
  "2015" = "#496B55",
  "2026 (so far)" = "#B65D50"
)

# 4. Create the comparison chart
p <- ggplot() +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0.5,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey50"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = past,
    aes(month_idx, nino34, color = label),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = now,
    aes(month_idx, nino34, color = label),
    linewidth = 2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = latest,
    aes(month_idx, nino34, color = label),
    size = 3
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = latest$month_idx[[1]],
    y = latest$nino34[[1]],
    label = sprintf(
      "%+.2f°C\n(%s)",
      latest$nino34[[1]],
      latest_month
    ),
    hjust = -0.15,
    vjust = 0.5,
    color = "#B65D50",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 15,
    y = 0.6,
    label = "+0.5°C reference",
    hjust = 1,
    vjust = 0,
    color = "grey40",
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = pal,
    breaks = names(pal)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = c(month.abb[7:12], month.abb[1:6]),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.20))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparing 2026 with past El Niño events",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Monthly Niño 3.4 anomalies, July-June. ",
      "2026 data through ", latest_month, "."
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Sea surface temperature anomaly (°C)",
    color = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Source: NOAA CPC, sstoi.indices;",
      "traditional monthly anomaly series."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(color = "#303B35"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.text = element_text(color = "#303B35"),
    plot.title = element_text(
      color = "#294638",
      face = "bold"
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#496B55"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#303B35"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#294638"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#496B55"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#EAF0EB", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#EAF0EB", color = NA)
  )

# Display chart
p

# Export slide-ready image
ggsave(
  "elnino_overlay.png",
  p,
  width = 10,
  height = 5.6,
  dpi = 200
)

# Optional: calculate the peak of each selected event
peaks <- df |>
  group_by(event) |>
  slice_max(nino34, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  transmute(
    event,
    peak_month = month.name[MON],
    peak_anomaly = round(nino34, 2)
  )

print(peaks)
```

```{r}

india_power <- tribble(
  ~category,      ~measure,        ~change,
  "Demand",       "Power demand",    24.3,
  "Generation",   "Coal",            20.7,
  "Generation",   "Solar + wind",     9.4,
  "Generation",   "Hydropower",      -6.3,
  "Generation",   "Gas",             -0.8
) |>
  mutate(
    category = factor(category, levels = c("Demand", "Generation")),
    measure = factor(
      measure,
      levels = c("Power demand", "Coal", "Solar + wind", "Hydropower", "Gas")
    )
  )

# Assign colors based on whether the value increased or decreased
india_power <- india_power |>
  mutate(
    direction = case_when(
      change < 0 ~ "Decrease",
      category == "Demand" ~ "Demand increase",
      TRUE ~ "Generation increase"
    )
  )

# Use these layers in your existing ggplot code
p <- ggplot(
  india_power,
  aes(x = change, y = measure, fill = direction)
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    color = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = sprintf("%+.1f", change),
      hjust = if_else(change >= 0, -0.2, 1.2)
    ),
    size = 4
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    category ~ .,
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Demand increase" = "#294638",
      "Generation increase" = "#77977B",
      "Decrease" = "#B65D50"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Change in average power (GW)",
    breaks = seq(-10, 30, by = 10),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.08, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "India's electricity demand and generation changes",
    subtitle = "June 2026 compared with June 2025",
    y = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Source: S&P Global figures reported by Business Standard,",
      "July 2026."
    )
  ) +
 theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(color = "#303B35"),
    plot.title = element_text(
      color = "#294638",
      face = "bold"
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#496B55"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#303B35"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#294638"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#496B55"),
    strip.text.y = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#294638"
    ),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(1, "lines"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#EAF0EB", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#EAF0EB", color = NA)
  )

p

ggsave(
  "india_june_power.png",
  p,
  width = 10,
  height = 5.6,
  dpi = 200
)

```
